results.name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and find a stable surface to hold onto for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and bring your heel towards your glutes. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand.
Keep your knees close together and lightly pull your right ankle upward, feeling a stretch along the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release your right ankle and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the left leg.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
results.description: Standing Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Standing Side Slope Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your posture upright. Raise your right arm overhead and allow your left hand to hang by your side.
Gently lean your torso to the left, reaching your right arm over your head and feeling a stretch along the right side of your torso.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, and slowly return to the starting position.
Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Ensure your shoulders remain relaxed and avoid tensing them up towards your ears.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
results.description: Standing Side Slope Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and place the heel of one foot on a low step or out in front of you with the leg straight.
Keep your back flat.
Hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch in the back of that leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep the standing knee soft.
Lead with your chest.
results.description: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Triceps Light Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and raise your right arm at chest height across your chest, bending your elbow.
Use your left hand to gently grab your right elbow, pulling it across your chest to deepen the stretch in your triceps.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch in your triceps.
Release the stretch and repeat with your left arm. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid twisting your torso; keep it stable and facing forward.
Breathe deeply and steadily, relaxing into the stretch.
Do not pull too hard; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
results.description: Triceps Light Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Upper Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, rounding your upper back and pushing your hands forward.
Lower both arms backward, bringing them to your sides just past behind your hips.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle squeeze in your upper back and shoulder blades.
Release and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe deeply and steadily, relaxing into the stretch.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders up towards your ears; keep them relaxed.
Do not overextend your arms; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
results.description: Upper Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Middle Back.

results.name: Band Skullcrusher
instructions: Attach one end of a loop resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing away from the anchor point. Hold the other end of the band with your hands in a neutral grip.
Lean forward slightly, allowing the band to extend. While hinging at the elbow joint, squeeze your triceps to straightening your arms. Hold for 1-2 seconds.
Slowly release the tension in the band, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms close to your head throughout the movement. Avoid letting your elbows flare outward during the extension.
Extend only at the elbows and keep your shoulders as still as possible.
Control the lowering phase to keep constant tension on the triceps.
Exhale as you straighten your arms and inhale as you return.
results.description: Band Skullcrusher is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms, Serratus Anterior.

results.name: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in the knees, facing the anchored resistance band.
Using an overhand grip, grasp the other end of the band, keeping your elbow bent and tucked close to your side.
Press downward by squeezing your triceps, extending your arm at the elbow joint. Pause briefly at the bottom of the exercise.
Slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired amount of repetitions and switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow close to your torso throughout the movement and upper arm stationary, moving only at the elbow joint.
Fully extend your arm without forcefully locking your elbow. Control the return phase to maintain constant tension on the band.
Stand tall with your chest up and core engaged to prevent body sway.
Exhale as you press downward and inhale as you return.
results.description: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Barbell Close Grip Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with your hands placed closer than shoulder-width apart, arms straight over your chest.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your triceps muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked in close to your body to engage your triceps effectively.
Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
results.description: Barbell Close Grip Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your elbows, bringing the barbell towards over your forehead.
When the barbell is behind your head, reverse the movement by extending your elbows to return the barbell to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment throughout the movement.
results.description: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Lying Triceps Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your elbows, bringing the barbell towards your forehead.
When the barbell is just above your forehead, reverse the movement by extending your elbows to return the barbell to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment throughout the movement.
results.description: Barbell Lying Triceps Skull Crusher is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
